name: Policies, handbooks, procedures and codes
one_line: The organizational situation of documents that state binding or authoritative RULES for an organisation's people and then govern themselves - policies, employee handbooks, codes of conduct, standard operating procedures and work instructions, together with their version history, approval records and the acknowledgements that prove people received them. The organizing anchor is the GOVERNING DOCUMENT as a controlled thing with an owner, an effective date and a review date, which separates it from the meeting that approved it and from the audit that tests whether it is followed. Absorbs the legacy rows ops.policy-handbook (ROW) and ops.process-documentation (FOLD) - a policy says what must happen and a procedure says how, and organisations keep them as one controlled set. Gist-level placeholder (J-IND): it recognizes the situation and writes NO field rows, because the business_operations schema declares none.

deterministic: PRECONDITION: every entry below is a DETECTION signal, never an extraction licence - this template's schema declares no field rows (PR-6; D1's deferral stands). “Privacy policy must be enforced before content reaches any model or external connector.”

a document-control block - a labelled table or header pairing a document owner or approver, a version, an effective or issue date, and a next-review date. This is the strongest single signal in the row and it is what makes a governing document a CONTROLLED document.

a normative-clause structure: numbered clauses in which obligation verbs recur - must, shall, is required to, may not - across a contents page of numbered sections. Prose alone does not do this; policies do it relentlessly.
a scope-and-application section naming who the document binds, followed by a definitions section - the standing opening shape of a policy.

a revision-history table listing versions, dates and a summary of change, usually at the front or the back. “Tables matter because resumes, forms, applications, invoices, and administrative documents often place their most useful information in cells rather than body paragraphs.”
an acknowledgement or attestation structure pairing one named individual, one named document version and a date or signature - the receipt side of the same situation.
a step-numbered procedure structure with responsibility columns, or a flowchart whose text layer carries step numbers and decision points - the work-instruction end of the set.
a distribution or circulation email whose labelled subject slot announces a new or updated policy and whose attachment-name slot names a handbook or policy document.
needs_llm: PRECONDITION: any model step runs after P7 and under the user's policy, and must abstain rather than guess: “A model that cannot cite sufficient evidence must return unknown.”

separating an organisation's OWN governing document from a copy of somebody else's - a supplier's policy filed as diligence evidence, a regulator's guidance, a downloaded template, a client's code imposed by contract. All four read identically. “Topic answers what a file is about, while purpose answers what the file was for.”
separating a policy from a contract: both are numbered obligation prose, and the difference is whether the document binds an organisation's people generally or two named parties to each other.
recognising a draft or a redline as belonging to the same governing document rather than as a separate document.
an undated, unversioned policy-shaped document with no control block - common in small organisations and the hardest real file here.

a purpose-coherent policy pack whose members are individually unremarkable - a handbook, three annexes, a signed acknowledgement sheet and a blank form. “The documents are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent.”
never_alone: the word policy, handbook, procedure, code or SOP in a filename alone. This is the tempting false file for this row: privacy policies of websites, insurance policies, downloaded templates and blog posts about policy all carry it, and an insurance policy is a finance document with no relation to this situation at all.
a version token alone - v3, Rev B, FINAL. Versioning is a universal fact (version family), not evidence of a governing document.
numbered clauses alone - contracts, standards, statutes and specifications are all numbered.

an organisation's name alone, read across by inference from “A university name alone should not create a group because Columbia can appear as an authoring school, course provider, target institution, employer, research venue, or merely a cited organization.”

an extension or a source_type alone - 00: “The engine should treat the file extension as a routing signal rather than an assumption about meaning, inspect the real MIME type or file signature where possible, and dispatch each file to a type-specific extractor.”
a bare 4-digit number read as an effective year, a policy number or a clause reference.

membership in a download session that dropped a whole policy library at once - “A session should never be treated as proof of topic, and it should not carry the same confidence as a hash match or a directly extracted document fact.”

work_types: code of conduct or ethics code
standard operating procedure or work instruction
grouping_reasons: one governing document across its versions and formats - the source document, the published PDF, the redline and the annexes - which is a version family before it is anything else.
one policy library or handbook set for one organisation at one effective date, held together by purpose rather than by content. “The documents are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent.”

one policy joined to the acknowledgement records collected for it, which is a real reason to group and the one most likely to tempt a named individual's employment status onto the policy itself. “The graph does not automatically copy those missing facts onto sparse files.”
no group at all is a valid outcome: a single downloaded template with no organisation and no control block is a standalone document, or reading material.

template.why: Empty by binding contract: business_operations declares no field rows (J-IND / PR-6, D1's deferral as narrowed, _CONTRACT rules 10 and 15), so no dimension can branch - a dimension naming an undeclared field opens a tree level no fact could ever fill. Held as prose for the pass that may license fields: the natural anchor is the organisation whose rules these are, then the policy AREA or function, then the governing document itself, with versions handled as a version family rather than as folder levels, because a version level would scatter one document across its own history. “The recommendation should follow the practical rule that a parent dimension should provide the context required to understand the child.” - a clause number or an annex is meaningless without the document, and the document is meaningless without the organisation, since the same policy title exists at every employer a person has ever had. Not time-first: “For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders.” - an effective date is a fact ABOUT a policy, not a home for it. Privacy caveat specific to this row: acknowledgement and attestation records are personnel records naming individuals, and they should not acquire automatic depth alongside the policy they attest to. “Protected branches should have configurable redaction in the canvas and review screens”. The user may reverse, remove or flatten any of this later; this is a recommendation, not a frozen filesystem.

collides_with.signal: The employee handbook is issued at induction and its acknowledgement is a joiner checklist item, so the same PDF sits in both situations. The discriminating evidence: a controlled governing document with an owner, a version and a review date supports this row; a checklist anchored on one named joiner spanning accounts, payroll and induction supports hr. Provenance: inference.

Policies are the evidence an audit collects, and an audit pack is largely a bundle of policies. The discriminating evidence: an audit or standard reference, a control identifier, a finding, or an auditor's request-list position supports the audit row; the governing document itself, with its control block, supports this row. Provenance: inference.

A code of conduct or policy annexed to and countersigned under a contract becomes a contractual instrument, and both documents are numbered obligation prose. The discriminating evidence: two named parties bound to each other, executed signature blocks, notice periods and an obligations register support contract administration; a document binding an organisation's people generally supports this row. Provenance: inference.

The word policy names a contract of insurance as readily as a governing document, and both are numbered clause documents with exclusions. The discriminating evidence: a policy number, an insured party, a premium, a period of cover and a schedule support the insurance row; a scope-and-application section, an owner, an effective date and a review date support this row. Provenance: inference.

Standard operating procedures and work instructions are the same document kind under two vocabularies, and the FOLD of ops.process-documentation into this row makes the overlap explicit. The discriminating evidence: a process, line, machine or product anchor with in-process controls supports the manufacturing row; an administrative or people-facing procedure supports this row. Provenance: inference.

Public-body policy work produces documents that look identical to internal governing documents and often carry the same words in their titles. The discriminating evidence: a public consultation, a legislative or rulemaking anchor, or an external audience supports the government row; a document binding one organisation's own people supports this row. Provenance: inference.

Policies are approved by boards and committees, so an approval record and a draft policy travel in the same board pack. The discriminating evidence: a notice, quorum, numbered papers or a resolution supports governance; the governing document itself supports this row. Provenance: inference.

falls_through_to.why: The home for a standalone policy, code or procedure with no accepted policy-library group around it. “Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.”

The correct home for a downloaded template, a regulator's guidance note or somebody else's policy saved for reference - material this row must not mistake for the organisation's own rules. “Reading Inbox may hold papers, articles, reports, and saved PDFs that appear to be reading material but have no active research, course, or project association.”

The cautious outcome for an undated, unversioned policy-shaped document whose ownership is unresolved. “Review Later may hold files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision.”

The correct home for acknowledgement and attestation records, which are personnel records naming individuals rather than governing documents. “Protected Records may represent sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials; it should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts.”

The safe outcome for a password-protected policy library archive or an unreadable document. “Unsupported or Encrypted may hold—or, more safely, represent without moving—password-protected archives, unreadable documents, damaged files, and unknown formats.”

sensitivity_why: The governing documents themselves are usually the least sensitive material in this family - many are published deliberately - but the situation is not separable from its acknowledgement and attestation side, which is a roster of named individuals joined to a compliance status, and from disciplinary and whistleblowing policies whose annexes carry case material. 00 names the corpus this product handles - it “can include identity documents, account statements, tax records, medical information, legal records, credentials, private correspondence, GPS metadata, employment materials, and educational records.” - and employment material is squarely in it. The operative limits are 00's: “Protected material should not be included in cloud-model prompts by default, should not display raw content in general group summaries, and should not be moved automatically without a user policy that explicitly permits it.”. The row takes the cautious value for the situation as a whole rather than assigning a lower one to the policy and a higher one to its receipts, because the two arrive together. This row assigns only the catalogue value potentially_sensitive; it does not assign, alias, rank, or infer a P7 handling class.
open_question: Whether the acknowledgement and attestation side should be split off into hr rather than kept here. Keeping it here makes the situation whole - a policy and the proof it was received are one controlled set, and that is how compliance functions actually file them - but it also means a row about rule documents carries a personnel roster, and the sensitivity value above is driven entirely by that half. Splitting it would give the governing documents a much lighter posture at the cost of breaking the set. The row does not resolve it, because the answer decides whether a policy library is ordinary or protected material for a real user.
